Can a salaried husband’s freelance income be shown in wife’s name for tax planning?

This is one of the most common family tax planning questions.

Example:
Freelance receipts: ₹24 Lakhs

If the same income is added to the husband’s salary income, the tax impact may go up substantially — even around ₹7.80 Lakhs in some cases.

But the real question is not “whose name is on the invoice?”

The real question is:

Who actually earned the income?

If the wife is only used as a name-lender, and the husband is doing all the work, then paperwork alone will not protect the case. The Income Tax Department may treat it as the husband’s income based on facts, bank trail, client communication, GST records and actual service delivery.

However, if the wife genuinely runs the freelance business, has relevant skills, signs contracts, delivers work, maintains a separate bank account, raises invoices, files GST/ITR properly and keeps full documentation, then it becomes a genuine business structure.

That is lawful tax planning.
A genuine structure can help with:
1.	Better family-level tax efficiency
2.	Cleaner documentation
3.	Lower scrutiny risk
4.	Proper compliance under Section 44ADA, if eligible
5.	Peace of mind during assessment

Key message:
Tax planning is legal.
Name-lending is risky.

Substance always matters more than paperwork.
